samples.summary: Scope creep: an issue-#1044 share-link UI parity change also flips the Yorkie auth webhook to enforce-by-default (plus a new backend service-token identity, READ_GATED_METHODS, ops-script secret plumbing). docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md scopes the work to N1–N8 (mount NotesToolbar, mobile demotion, viewer toolbar, share-token uploader, divider hit area, doc corrections) and explicitly lists what is out of scope; none of the backend authorization work is in it. The flip is also the step docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md said to defer: its Goals still read "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)" (line 43, unchanged by this diff) and the old verb risk said to "watch the shadow logs" and confirm viewer attach/PushPull verbs before enforcing. The branch's own notes (docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:76-85) record an unverified question — whether a viewer's later presence-only change counts toward pack.HasChanges() and therefore makes PushPull `rw` — and say it "is the thing to watch first in the shadow-mode rollout window", while this same change removes that window as the default. If that question resolves the wrong way, viewer share links break sync on every deployment that registers the methods and configures nothing else.
samples.evidence: isYorkieAuthEnforced: `return raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'` shipped alongside a notes-toolbar issue; yorkie-auth-webhook.md Goals line 43 still states shadow-before-enforce; lessons doc defers the presence/HasChanges verification to "the shadow-mode rollout window".

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim second copy of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` (`readOnlyDocStore`): same reader-allowlist rationale, same Proxy traps (get/set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions/isExtensible/has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys), same non-configurable-property carve-out, same memoization. Only the reader list, the `undo`/`redo` null return, and a new idempotency WeakSet differ — i.e. the two copies have already diverged on the first day. This repo expects reuse (shared code in `@wafflebase/core`; see docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md), and a generic `readOnlyStoreView(store, readers, overrides)` would have served both. As written, a fix or hardening of one proxy's traps will not reach the other, and the two engines' viewer mounts get different boundaries.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-168 vs packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:117-185 — trap-for-trap identical bodies; only docs lacks the READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotency guard.

samples.summary: A comment added by this very change states the opposite of the policy the same change ships: "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either". This PR makes enforcement the default (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`) and the design doc/notes.md go out of their way to record the old claim as wrong. New rationale that contradicts the branch's own decision is how the next reader re-derives a false premise.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:446-448 (added in this diff) vs docs/design/notes/notes.md "What that wrapper is not" and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:28-32.

samples.summary: Design-doc discipline: the default flip is only partly propagated. docs/design/README.md's index row for yorkie-auth-webhook.md still advertises a "shadow→enforce rollout", and yorkie-auth-webhook.md's own Goals bullet (line 43) still lists "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)" even though the Rollout section now says a new deployment goes straight to enforce. The canonical doc therefore states both postures.

The docs package still carries the claim this change declares false: `readOnlyDocStore`'s doc comment says the webhook "ships in shadow mode by default … so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary", and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413 repeats it. The notes twin added here explicitly retracts that reasoning, so the repo now holds two contradictory statements about the same deployment default. The change that flipped the default is the change that owed the correction.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42; packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413; contrast packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts "What that wrapper is not".

samples.summary: The PdfCollabProvider behaviour change (`initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`) is not reflected in its canonical design doc: pdf.md still says the `comments` map is "seeded empty at bootstrap via initialRoot … never created lazily — see the convergence note in Slice 2", which is now untrue for a viewer mount. Additionally, the other four types express this rule as a `*InitialRootForRole` helper in `packages/frontend/src/types/*-document.ts`; pdf inlines a ternary in the component instead of adding `pdfInitialRootForRole` next to `initialPdfRoot`, so the one rule now has two shapes.

The same env var now has two incompatible readings in one repo: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` treats unset as enforcing, while `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (and register-templates.ts) demand the literal `'true'`. The divergence is argued in comments, but the operator-facing consequence is that a deployment that *is* enforcing (variable unset, methods registered) is told "The public template gallery requires YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true" — one variable meaning "honour my denials" in one place and "I attest the methods are registered" in another. If the second question is the real one, it wants its own variable rather than a second reading of this one.

The fix for "the two notes entry paths differ" re-implements the workspace route's state machine a second time rather than sharing it: `viewMode`/`keymap`/`showAuthors` state, the `readViewMode`/`readKeymap`/`readShowAuthors` seeding and the identical `isMobile && viewMode === 'both' ? 'edit'` demotion all exist in `app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:90-119` too. A small `useNotesViewState({ persist })` hook would have kept the two paths in lockstep; as written the next mode/keymap addition has to be remembered twice — the exact divergence issue #1044 is about.

Unrelated-to-issue hunks ride along: the two docs-package test teardown fixes (undisposed editors leaving a cursor-blink interval firing against a torn-down jsdom) are a CI-flake fix in a different package from the notes share-link work and the backend authorization work. Harmless, but it makes the change's scope a third thing.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31 returns enforce-for-anything-but-literal-'false', with its comment declaring "Enforcing is the default" and describing the new READ_GATED_METHODS / service-token machinery. Sibling review artifacts (.agent-review/docs/summary.md:3, .agent-review/test-adequacy/verdict.json:21-36) confirm the flip, the service token, and the README/self-hosting prose edits belong to this same change set, while the originating task doc (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:12-58) scopes the work to N1-N8 plus divider/doc corrections and names only Sheets/Board toolbars as out of scope — no backend authorization work anywhere in it. The design doc Goals bullet at yorkie-auth-webhook.md:43 is verbatim as quoted, and the lessons doc (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:78-85) records the deciding question as unverified and defers it to "the shadow-mode rollout window" that this change removes as the default, while lines 99-101 confirm the branch itself made enforce the default. The finding does overstate one point — the design doc's Status (:24-32), Rollout (:213-225) and Risks (:240-250, :270-306) were substantively rewritten to document and justify enforce-by-default, so only the stale Goals bullet contradicts it, and design-doc discipline was met. That does not refute the scope mismatch or its cost: an unverified verb question gating viewer PushPull is left carrying a deployment-posture flip bundled into a share-link UI PR, and other active docs (20260902-revision-history-todo.md:274, 20260902-template-gallery-public-tier-todo.md:251) still describe shadow as the default. No named refutation ground applies.
